finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could supply a specially crafted input that causes atoi to return an unexpected value, leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
finding.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not handle invalid input gracefully.

finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: An attacker could supply a very large value for N, causing integer overflow and leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
finding.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not check for overflow conditions.

finding.title: Improper Release of Resources
finding.trigger: An attacker could supply a very large value for N, causing the creation of a large number of child processes, leading to resource exhaustion.
finding.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not limit the number of child processes created.

finding.title: Lack of Error Handling
finding.trigger: An attacker could supply invalid input that causes atoi to return an unexpected value, leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
finding.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not handle invalid input gracefully.
